_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 2.3. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Under s. 57 Firearms Act 1968, a 'firearm' includes…
options: A lethal barrelled weapon, prohibited weapons, component parts and noise/flash moderators

questions.scenario: What is an 'imitation firearm'?
options: Anything which has the appearance of a firearm, whether or not it can discharge anything

questions.scenario: D robs a shop with his fingers pointed under his jacket, pretending to have a gun. Following R v Bentham, is it an imitation firearm?
options: No – a part of the body is not a 'thing' that can be possessed
Only if the victim believed it

questions.scenario: Which of these is a prohibited weapon under s. 5?
options: A starting pistol that can't fire

questions.scenario: Which offence under the Firearms Act does NOT include imitation firearms?
options: s. 16 – possession with intent to endanger life

questions.scenario: D uses a replica gun to make a police officer back off so he can escape arrest. Which offence?
options: s. 17(1) – using a firearm or imitation to resist or prevent arrest

questions.scenario: D commits a burglary with a real but unloaded pistol in his pocket, never showing it. Which firearms offence?
options: s. 17(2) – possessing a firearm/imitation at the time of committing a Schedule 1 offence
explanations: No intent to endanger life shown.

questions.scenario: What is the maximum penalty for s. 18 (having firearm with intent to commit indictable offence)?
Under s. 16A, D possesses a firearm or imitation with intent to…
options: Cause someone to believe that unlawful violence will be used against them or another

questions.scenario: For s. 19 (carrying in a public place), which item counts only if LOADED?
A youth has an unloaded air rifle in a park without reasonable excuse. Is it a s. 19 offence?
options: Yes – air weapons count loaded or not

questions.scenario: D carries an unloaded handgun in the street with no ammunition. Is it s. 19?
options: No – for 'other firearms' he must have suitable ammunition with him (but s. 5 possession applies)

questions.scenario: Who bears the burden of proving 'lawful authority or reasonable excuse' under s. 19?
D was released 2 years ago from a 4-year prison sentence and is found with a shotgun. Which is correct?
options: s. 21 offence – a sentence of 3 years or more means a lifetime prohibition
Only if he has no certificate

questions.scenario: A person sentenced to 6 months' imprisonment may not possess a firearm for…
Under s. 47, what can an officer do if he has reasonable cause to suspect a person has a firearm in a public place?
options: Require him to hand it over for examination, search and detain him, and stop and search a vehicle

questions.scenario: D enters a house as a trespasser carrying an imitation firearm. Which offence?
options: s. 20 – trespassing with a firearm or imitation in a building

questions.scenario: Since 1997, which category became generally prohibited under s. 5?
What is the key requirement for a s. 1 firearm?
Which is an important safety principle when dealing with a reported armed suspect?
options: Contain and await authorised firearms officers; preserve forensic evidence

questions.scenario: A replica gun is used in a robbery of a bank. Which firearms offence is most directly charged with the robbery?
Is a silencer (sound moderator) itself a 'firearm'?
options: Yes – accessories designed to diminish noise or flash are included
